Hey pal, can I pick your brain if you don't mind? UJ recent price action has got me in a bit of a muddle.

I've annotated this chart with how I was reading things, with numbered points. The most important recent action around an FTR seemed like (2), but actually a more minor one (to my thinking) ended up holding price down strongly.

Am I simply "expecting" price to behave in a certain manner too much?

Certainly, after the long LF/FTR from the engulf of level (2) got engulfed itself, that was a clue to look short for the near term, but I thought one of the the 2 long FLs/FTRs shown (the one above my note (5) seemed a strong one, the one below note (5) is what I'm seeing as the beginning of the up move) would have caused a big bounce up in price, up to the higher zone at (4).

HTF was definitely bearish, coming off monthly supply - in these circumstances, is it quite often the case that an "unexpected" level (but still technically valid) can turn price in the direction of HTF (even after a seemingly important opposing FTR was taken out at (2) in this case), and we've just got to go with what we can see, favouring HTF direction?

I just want to get this down to a science, and not get caught out by these kinds of things, but maybe I'm expecting too much to be trying to look for and hold longs against HTF. Perhaps I need a mental rule "when HTF is going a certain direction, don't expect the obvious level to be the one it turns at - just go with what you can see, and hold bets in direction of HTF for as long as you get PA"

Cheers for any assistance.
